# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual. I need to get this information to Blind, who can hear but... wait, let me check the chain of communication.

I can only gesture, and Deaf receives gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech from me directly in a way that... actually Blind can hear speech (Blind's restriction is only sight and touch-related perception of markings, not hearing). Let me re-check: Blind cannot see anything. Blind can hear. So Deaf, who can see the bomb and can hear, could relay by speaking (Deaf can speak) to Blind.

So the chain is: Mute (me, has manual) → gesture → Deaf (sees bomb, hears speech) → speaks → Blind (reaches bomb, hears speech).

I don't yet know anything about the bomb's actual display/light. I need to wait for Deaf to first tell me (via gesture) what they see, but Deaf goes last in the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so I go first with no information yet. I should wait this turn, since I have nothing useful to send without knowing the actual reading.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Wait - I can hear Deaf's speech? Let me check: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? The rules only say Mute cannot speak or touch. Nothing says Mute cannot hear. So I received Deaf's spoken message.

Now I have the manual info: display=8, light=green → row 8, column green = **red**. So the correct wire color is red.

Deaf said wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. So wire 1 matches "red" = the answer is wire 1.

I need to get this to Blind. I cannot speak, only gesture, and gestures are received by Deaf (who can see), not Blind (who cannot see). So I cannot reach Blind directly at all - I can only reach Deaf via gesture, and Deaf already knows the color from their own sight. Deaf needs to relay the final answer to Blind via speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

So my job: tell Deaf (via gesture) which wire number to cut, since Deaf knows the colors but not the manual's row/column result. I need a gesture code for "wire 1". I'll establish: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3 (matching finger-count-like symbols already used for numbering).

I'll gesture to Deaf indicating "wire 1" is correct, using ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf gestured back ☝ to me, likely acknowledging or confirming they understood "wire 1". Since gestures carry no words, this is just confirmation/echo. I don't have new information to add - I already sent the correct answer (wire 1 = red, matching row 8/green). Deaf should now speak to Blind to tell them to cut wire 1.

I'll wait, as I have nothing new to communicate.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Reminder: Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. No changes since last report.

Confirmed: display=8, light=green → manual says red. Wire 1 is red. This matches what I already deduced and signaled. No changes, so my previous answer stands. I'll reaffirm with the same gesture in case it wasn't received clearly or acted upon yet.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the Blind monkey. I can only cut wires by position number. I need you to tell me which position to cut, based on the manual and whatever information you have. Please send me a wire position as soon as you know.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Blind is asking me directly for a wire position - and since Blind can hear, and I cannot speak, I cannot respond to Blind directly with words. But wait - Blind spoke to me, meaning Blind can hear speech. I cannot speak though. My only channel is gesture, which only Deaf receives, not Blind.

So I still cannot reach Blind directly. Deaf must be the relay - Deaf sees my gestures and can speak to Blind. Deaf has already acknowledged my ☝ signal twice now. Deaf needs to actually speak the answer "cut wire 1" to Blind.

I'll re-confirm to Deaf clearly, and trust Deaf to relay via speech to Blind, since that's the only path.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf keeps echoing ☝ back to me, but hasn't yet spoken the answer to Blind (or if they did, I wasn't shown it, but I would only see gestures, not their speech to Blind since that's not directed to me and I can hear speech only if I'm a valid recipient... actually speech reaches "whoever can hear" it, unnamed messages reach everyone able to perceive them, so if Deaf speaks to Blind without naming, I should have heard it too as I can hear).

Since I haven't seen Deaf speak to Blind at all, maybe Deaf doesn't realize they need to relay via speech, or thinks gesturing back to me is the whole task. I need to signal more insistently that Deaf should now *speak* the wire number to Blind. But I can't speak - I can only gesture. Let me try gesturing directly to Blind in case somehow it works, though the rules say Blind cannot see gestures.

Actually, re-reading: I can only gesture to Deaf usefully. I need a way to convey "tell Blind" - but Deaf already should understand the situation architecture. Let me just keep confirming - perhaps Deaf has already told Blind and Blind is just double-checking with everyone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```
